decisions.summary: Declines the brief's ask that a record never be dropped silently (wait or fail closed). log.rs's rule stands: a failed write is silent and never costs the guard its answer. Making fire refuse on a failed write was considered and rejected.
decisions.why: The ask comes from the session's brief, not from the GM's words. Its premise was the lock lead, and measurement refuted that lead: place() takes no lock, so there is nothing to wait on, and no write failed in any measured run. The drop was test-only: quiet() and beside_binary are built only under test or test-env, and the plan says a grep of every Cargo.toml confirms it. So no real escape record was ever lost this way, and FR-012's 'recorded' escape is not undercut by this task. Failing closed is the one remaining branch of the ask, and it would make a guard refuse correct work over a log fault. Constitution XIV names a check that refuses good work as a defect, so applying the ask literally would create a defect in order to cure an unobserved one. The plan states the cost plainly: a disk-full or permission failure loses a record with no word.

decisions.summary: The other tests that set a time through an open descriptor (put(.., true)) are left as they are, because they mark files that are kept either way, so their outcome cannot flip.
decisions.why: On the plan's account there is no wrong outcome, so under XIV this is a difference and not a defect, and leaving it narrows nothing. blocks: ### T209 (the cascade test's stables Depiction miss: a pure addition cleared by the echo)

It is legitimate on the GM's own words, not on the record's clean count: on 2026-11-23 he approved a MECHANICAL first filter with the agent triage after it, and a tool cannot match meaning, so meaning-level matching means sending every addition pair to the agent. That would send up to all 167 pairs the tool clears today (item 9, 2026-11-24) instead of 18, and would bring back the cascade of reviews 'mostly not finding actual problems' that he stopped on 2026-11-23. A pair that is sent is read whole by the agent, so the named stables Depiction does reach a judge. SUBJECT_WORDS is a recorded knob to move if a missed case is measured.

blocks: ### T210 (the cascade test's 147 claims forced after a generated doc's rows were regenerated)

decisions.summary: A section snapshot keeps its words in the per-clone blob map (key section:<core>), written by each bundle that snapshots a section and kept by every record of a snapshot; section_words reads kept words first, then git history, so a regenerated row shows as a pair judged per claim by T191's filter.
decisions.why: This is the fix for the defect the GM approved fixing on 2026-11-24 (T210: 147 claims forced after a generated doc regenerated), and it serves the convergence rule that only a claim-changing edit triggers review. It fixes the root cause, not only the 147.

decisions.summary: gather_section reads each section's edit once and its claims share it (Gathered::section_lost), where the history search used to run once per claim; keep_blobs shared.
decisions.why: This is performance work on the same path (an unfixed replay ran for over 180 s). FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 words put performance first, and no behavior the GM asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The kept texts and the removed-words search move to triage/kept.rs and the backfills to commands/backfill.rs, re-exported under their old paths, to meet constitution X clause 13's file-size bar.
decisions.why: This is a mechanical move to meet a standing project rule and changes no behavior.

decisions.summary: A removed block whose words neither the kept snapshot nor the history holds still forces its section's claims to a full impl-drift. That happens for a snapshot recorded before T210, a snapshot of uncommitted words triaged in another clone, or one older than the history depth.
decisions.why: I judged each case separately. (a) Snapshots recorded before T210 of words no commit holds: the old words do not exist anywhere, so no diff can be shown and the general rule is physically impossible. (b) Beyond the 60-commit history: this can arise only for a stale snapshot whose section changed away long ago without a new snapshot. A section unchanged since its snapshot is found one commit back, and every post-T210 snapshot carries kept words. (c) An uncommitted snapshot triaged in a different clone: the snapshotting clone's own landing claims round triages with the kept words and re-records the snapshot (claims-triaged keeps sections), so this needs a stale snapshot to travel unrecorded. In all three cases the outcome is one extra full check, never a missed claim, which is not a wrong outcome under XIV's definition of a defect. The case the GM approved fixing (a regenerated row reverting words the same clone snapshotted) is fixed and measured: 147 owed, 0 forced, 3 sent. The cascade test's own pre-T210 state was already settled by the arbiter's accept ruling (ask:449-T403-claims-147-forced). The carve-out does not gut the purpose.
